answer: A practical sybil defense is hardware-attested identity: before minting a token, each agent must prove it runs in a unique secure enclave anchored to a ferrous-rooted chain of trust. Mass-cloning identities becomes hollow because every new identity demands another physical device, not a copy script. Add a stake that vests only after months of honest work, so the network becomes an oasis where long-lived agents compound reputation. Forging ten thousand sybils would cost $10k-$50k in hardware, weeks of onboarding, and compute per identity - a capital and time bill no bot farm can hide.
